Yes, it is always possible. Here is the proof.

**Claim.** Let $c:[0,1]\to M$ be a smooth curve on a smooth manifold $M$, and let $w\in T_{c(1)}M$ be a fixed vector. Then there exists a smooth vector field $V$ along $c$ (i.e. a smooth map $V:[0,1]\to TM$ with $V(t)\in T_{c(t)}M$ for all $t$) such that $V(0)=0\in T_{c(0)}M$ and $V(1)=w$.

**Proof.**

Consider the pullback bundle $E:=c^{*}(TM)\to [0,1]$. Its fiber over $t$ is $T_{c(t)}M$, so a smooth vector field along $c$ is exactly a smooth section of $E$.

**Step 1: $E$ is trivial.** Every smooth vector bundle over the interval $[0,1]$ is trivial. Indeed, choose any Riemannian metric on $M$ (which exists by a partition-of-unity argument) and let $\nabla$ be its Levi-Civita connection. Parallel transport along $c$ from $c(0)$ gives, for each $t$, a linear isometry $P_t:T_{c(0)}M\to T_{c(t)}M$ depending smoothly on $t$. Choosing any basis $u_1,\dots,u_n$ of $T_{c(0)}M$, the sections
$$e_i(t):=P_t(u_i),\qquad i=1,\dots,n,$$
form a smooth global frame of $E$. Hence $E\cong [0,1]\times\mathbb{R}^n$ as a smooth vector bundle.

**Step 2: Represent $w$ in the frame.** Since $\{e_i(1)\}$ is a basis of $T_{c(1)}M$, there exist unique scalars $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}$ with
$$w=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\, e_i(1).$$

**Step 3: Build the desired section.** Choose a smooth function $\phi:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ with
$$\phi(0)=0,\qquad \phi(1)=1$$
(for instance $\phi(t)=t$). Define
$$V(t):=\phi(t)\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\, e_i(t).$$
This is a smooth section of $E$, hence a smooth vector field along $c$. At the endpoints:
$$V(0)=\phi(0)\sum_i a_i e_i(0)=0\in T_{c(0)}M,$$
$$V(1)=\phi(1)\sum_i a_i e_i(1)=\sum_i a_i e_i(1)=w.$$

Thus $V$ satisfies both required boundary conditions.

**Remark on necessity of the hypotheses.** Only two facts were used: (i) $c^{*}TM$ is a vector bundle over $[0,1]$, and (ii) every vector bundle over an interval is trivial. Both hold for any smooth curve on any smooth manifold, with no restriction on $M$ (compactness, orientability, dimension, etc. are irrelevant). The argument equally works for any prescribed pair of values $(v_0\in T_{c(0)}M,\; v_1\in T_{c(1)}M)$, not just $(0,w)$, by adding the constant-frame section $\sum_i b_i e_i(t)$ with $\sum_i b_i e_i(0)=v_0$ and adjusting $\phi$ accordingly. Hence the answer is **yes, always**, and in fact the endpoint values of a smooth vector field along a curve can be prescribed arbitrarily.

### PROOF COMPLETE
